# 大乘起信論裂網疏

**ID:** T1850
**Volume:** T44
**Category:** 論集部類
**Original Category:** 論疏部
**Byline:** 明 智旭述
**Dynasty:** 明
**Date:** 1653
**Juans:** 6
**CBETA:** https://cbetaonline.dila.edu.tw/zh/T1850

## Contributors
- 智旭 (A001257)

## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A six-*juǎn* commentary on the *Dà-shèng qǐ-xìn lùn* — specifically, on the Tang [實叉難陀](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AF%A6%E5%8F%89%E9%9B%A3%E9%99%80) Śikṣānanda translation [KR6o0079](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6o/KR6o0079) (T32n1667), not the more familiar Liáng-Paramārtha translation. By [智旭](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%99%BA%E6%97%AD) Ǒu-yì Zhì-xù 蕅益智旭 (1599–1655), one of the *Wǎn-Míng sì dà gāosēng* 晚明四大高僧 (the four great masters of late Ming Buddhism). The image in the title — *liè-wǎng* 裂網, "rending the net [of false views]" — frames the commentary as a polemical clearing of mistaken interpretations rather than a sequential gloss.

**Abstract**

The text opens with the author's identification: 靈峰蕅益沙門智旭述 ("composed by the monk Zhìxù of Língfēng [Mountain], [styled] Ǒuyì"). The opening doctrinal preface is a classic statement of Zhìxù's integrative position: "The path of the Buddhas and patriarchs is the transmission of mind through mind. The bodhisattvas' composition of treatises and exposition of sūtras is also for this one great matter alone. Thus it says: 'Searching the ten directions one finds no other vehicle.' Even when the teachings are bent down to the various capacities and gradually lead the disciples — using the provisional in service of the real, expounding the various paths — they are like the three kinds of grass and two kinds of trees that receive the same rain unequally; yet the rain that moistens them is of one taste."

Zhì-xù's distinctive contribution to the *Qǐ-xìn lùn* tradition is twofold. First, he is virtually alone among major commentators in working from Śikṣānanda's translation rather than Paramārtha's, on the conviction that the Śikṣānanda is closer to the (assumed) Sanskrit original. Second, he reads the *Qǐ-xìn lùn* not through a Huáyán *xìng-qǐ* lens (as [法藏](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%B3%95%E8%97%8F) had done) nor through a Yogācāra-only lens (as [太賢](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%A4%AA%E8%B3%A2)), but through his characteristic *Tiāntái* 天台-Yogācāra-Pure Land synthesis. Composition is bracketed by Zhì-xù's late-career commentarial period at Língfēng-sì, c. 1646–1655.
